bg: The author was "Judas, the brother of James" the Less (Jude 1:1), called also Lebbaeus (Matt. 10:3) and Thaddaeus (Mark 3:18). The genuineness of this epistle was early questioned, and doubts regarding it were revived at the time of the Reformation; but the evidences in support of its claims are complete.

In Jude 1:9 mention is made of a contention between Michael and the devil about the body of Moses. This dispute is supposed to have had reference to the concealment of the body of Moses so as to prevent idolatry.
ch.s: This chapter covers: The apostle exhorts to stedfastness in the faith (vv. 1–4); The danger of being infected by false professors, and the dreadful punishment which shall be inflicted on them and their followers (vv. 5–7); An awful description of these seducers and their deplorable end (vv. 8–16); Believers cautioned against being surprised at such deceivers arising among them (vv. 17–23); The epistle ends with an encouraging doxology, or words of praise (vv. 24,25). People named: James, Moses, Cain, Balaam, Enoch, Adam. Places: Egypt, Sodom.
ch.mh: Christians are called out of the world, from the evil spirit and temper of it; called above the world, to higher and better things, to heaven, things unseen and eternal; called from sin to Christ, from vanity to seriousness, from uncleanness to holiness; and this according to the Divine purpose and grace.
q: Read verses 1–4 (The apostle exhorts to stedfastness in the faith). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 5–7 (The danger of being infected by false professors, and the dreadful punishment which shall be inflicted on them and their followers), what do you learn about grace and mercy?
Verse 24 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside 2 Timothy 4:18. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
What does James’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of salvation and redemption in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of Jude?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: Let us more often look up to Him who is able to keep us from falling, to improve as well as maintain the work he has wrought in us, till we shall be presented blameless before the presence of his glory.
ch.a: Show the same mercy you have received to someone who does not deserve it.
